utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that members of the Dutch Battalion checked in order to make sure that the people from Srebrenica were not moving anywhere they wanted to?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because of this barrier between the civilians and the Army of Republika Srpska, is it correct that VRS soldiers were not -- did not have any contact with the civilians before members of the DutchBat would let civilians through in order to get to the buses?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No, that's not true, because in the end while we were a human cordon, we saw that man that I later saw executed be removed from that crowd by the VRS. So that means that ultimately they couldn't -- we weren't capable of keeping them separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in that cordon, sometimes you were in front of and sometimes you were behind the armed Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: In front of and among, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the armed members of the Serb formations arrived, did you move around Potocari on your own or were you always in a group? And mean I you personally.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I was primarily in a group, but a few times I was alone within -- within view of the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the farthest that you ventured out away from the group?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you just give us an idea? What is it 5 metres, 10 metres, a hundred metres, a kilometre way away?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Let's say it was between 20 and 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, it's time for the break. Could I first ask the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in the meanwhile, where are we, not in terms of minutes, but in terms of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Over one-half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Over one-half. Yes. Then we'll take the break, and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber was informed there was a preliminary matter to be raised. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, I was able to clear up in speaking with Mr. Lukic the example he used of my reference in questioning the witness, and I simply can tell you what Mr. Lukic was reading from was me reading a 92 ter summary of the Popovic testimony of this witness, and that's where I had said that this -- he acknowledged that he had not mentioned in any previous statement that the Muslim population who refused to get on the buses were first insulted and then forced onto the buses. That was me providing a complete statement for that Court. Now, where I got that was in Blagojevic trial where Mr. Karnavas had brought that fact out through the witness in cross at page 1038. So apparently Mr. Lukic picked me over Mr. Karnavas but Mr. Karnavas was the -- actually brought the evidence out. I was just repeating it in a 92 ter summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One thing may be clear, I was a bit concerned about it being a 92 ter summary because that's not evidence. Let that be clear, and I also had specific reasons, therefore, to see whether there was any way to verify that, which now apparently Mr. McCloskey has explained to us where the quote came from. I -- yes, I leave it to that at this moment. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. I notice, Mr. Mladic, that you were speaking very much aloud when we entered the courtroom. I didn't know what you said, but let it be clear that the instruction is no loud speaking when the Chamber is there. I repeat that at this moment and leave it to that, not knowing yet what you said. If that would ever come to my knowledge, then we'll further consider whether this is the right approach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you said you were halfway. In terms of time, you are a little bit beyond halfway in your time estimate. Could you please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You testified about a man who was executed. Today on page 8 of the transcript you told us about this, but I would like to ask you now this: How many people -- how many armed people were there around that man who was executed, as you said?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Of the three men surrounding him, I know that in any case the man who shot were armed, and I can't say that with any certainty about the other two.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Other than the executed man and these three men surrounding him, was there any one else in their vicinity?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could we clarify what means "in the vicinity"? Earlier you asked even for whether 1 kilometre was still in view. So therefore "vicinity" is even more vague. Other not being in the vicinity, at what distance were they approximately, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there was nobody else in the vicinity at 30 to 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were there people on the road.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, did you inform anyone on the same day of the incident?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who did you report this to, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Initially I reported it to a sergeant of mine, and he told me that I should notify Lieutenant Schotman about that. The translation of the name is not entirely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One will still work on it. I can see that from the little sign, but I take it that what you wanted to pronounce is S-c-h-o-t-m-a-n, or is it with an S mental middle? Schotman or Schotsman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Schotman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we are. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We uploaded in e-court the Tolimir portion. That's 1D909, which contains a quote from the Blagojevic case. We need page 39 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were asked whether you had reported that to your superiors at this trial as well, and you replied, and I will quote now from page 9 and on: [In English] "A. That evening, I reported for the first time on that indent, and that has been noted in the official document. "Q. Thank you. So there is an official document in respect of that. "Now, in the Blagojevic case on page 1036, lines 10 through 13, the Blagojevic/Jokic case, in response to the Prosecution's question and I quoted his question: "'Did you at any time have occasion to report what you had seen?' "In reply to that you said, I quote: "'No, not on the same day.' "And then when you were asked when in line 15 you said: "'On the next morning.' "So which of the two is correct, what you have stated today or what you stated in Blagojevic/Jokic case? Thank you. "A. Thank you to have freshened my memory. It is true that I only reported the next morning." [Interpretation] So what is correct? What was it that you reported and when?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: It first came up that evening, and I was asked to write down the official version the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what you said in the Blagojevic case, that you did not report anything on the first day but, rather, only on the following day, is not correct?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: The official report did indeed come about only the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As I understood this in line 15 of the Tolimir transcript, page 1204, you were asked whether at any point in time you had the opportunity to report what you had seen, and you said: "No, not on that day. On the next morning." There is no mention here, would you agree with me, that you reported this incident in any manner on that same day?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I see that some unclarity has indeed arisen about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember whether Major Franken was informed of this?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You described the armed Serbs, so I'd like to ask you whether it is correct that even these men who surrounded the men who had been executed, as you said, wore different camouflage uniforms, that the colours were different and the patterns were different on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: I couldn't say anything about that now. Do you mean whether those three men were different?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were dressed differently.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No, not as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 1D908, please, page -- pages 56 and 57, which should be pages 3013 and 3014 of your evidence in the Popovic case on the 25th of October, 2006. I will read this portion out in English. That's line 25 on page 1 where I begin. We need line 25, and then we will move over to the next page: [In English] "Q. Later on you were asked to describe the four soldiers whom you say you saw carry out an execution, and you gave this description at page 1035: 'It was camouflage in various shades, various colours.' Did you mean by that that the soldiers were, each of them, wearing different sorts of uniform, different camouflages? "A. That is correct. "Q. And rather like the soldiers that you saw arrive first at Potocari, they didn't appear to you to be like ordinary soldiers? "A. To me, ordinary soldiers are people recognisable by wearing the same attire, and that certainly did not hold true for these men."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This quotation raises the issue of whether you saw three men taking part in the murder or four men taking part in the murder.

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: As is apparent, I remember only three, but apparently there were four. That's the consequence of years passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now take a look again at 1D908, e-court page 7 and page 8. We'll start with page 92 -- 2964 in the Popovic case of 25 October 2006. We need line 25, and then we will move over onto the next page: [In English] "Q. When you first saw that man, the civilian man, in the crowd with Serb soldiers around him, how many Serb soldiers did you see around him in the crowd? "A. Four. "Q. Okay. And when you saw the man shot, how many Serb soldiers were standing around him then? "A. There were also four."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you agree with me that you hadn't seen this incident at all? Rather, perhaps you heard about it from someone else?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: That's your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were not present during this incident that you described?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These four men or these three men, today you say that you don't know whether they had been armed or not, all three of them. You say that you saw one armed man. Were they armed? What about the fourth person? Who is he? Do you remember that today at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which question do you want the witness to answer,

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Were they armed? What about the fourth person? Who is he? Do you remember that today at all?" Which of the four questions do you want him to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I suggest you take them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you remember the fourth man today, or do you not remember him at all?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No. As it became clear earlier, my memory turned them into three but apparently there were four. And at the incident I was only focusing on the man who shot, so he is the only one that I can say for certain had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page -- actually, you're not sure at all today whether the other two or three men had been armed?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No. That true. The focus was entirely and purely on the man who shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 3014, which is page 58 in e-court of this same transcript -- I do apologise. We need page 57, and it corresponds to page 3014 of the transcript of your testimony on the 25th of October, 2006. This is how the question starts, I'll read it from line 11. [In English] I quote: "Q. Is it also the case that there seems to be some confusion between these four men as to what they were to do and as to who was to carry out the shooting? "A. As far as I'm concerned, all I can do is suggest, because I don't know the language and I don't know what those men were saying to each other, but it seemed to me that they were hesitating as to who would fire the shot. " [Interpretation] Is it correct that we see from this testimony of yours that you testified then that if not all of them were armed, several of them were at any rate because there was this dilemma as to who would shoot; right?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At this point in time, can you tell us with any certainty how many of the men there were armed or not? Can you not say that today?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No. I'm truly sorry, but I simply can't remember exactly how many men had how many weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was anybody else from the Dutch Battalion present there where you were, and did anybody else see that killing?

utterances.speaker: PAUL GROENEWEGEN
utterances.text: No. That was because I had strayed from the road further down alone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, again these are two questions in one. Can we separate them? Witness, I do understand that from your answer that no other DutchBat member was present where you were. That is an answer to the first question. The second is whether anyone, any other DutchBat member, even not being present at where you were, could have seen the murder.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's true that I can't answer that second question. All I know from others is that they did not see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were there any persons within such a distance that they could have possibly seen it despite of whether you can confirm that they did or did not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. There were no other people nearby at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that you say that from a distance of 30 to 50 metres you cannot see someone being killed? Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I can't say anything about that. I know where I was standing, and that's what I estimate the distance was from where I was standing up to the incident, and who else was around, there were certainly spots from where people could have seen it, but that would be guessing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see whether there's not even more confusion than -- one second, please. I understood your previous answer about the 13 -- 30 to 50 metres to be an answer to the question at what distance persons were closest to the event, apart from you, which you say was 30 to 50 metres. Now, your last answer has confused me, because it seems to suggest that you yourself were at a distance of 30 to 50 metres. If that is the case, then please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's very difficult for me to estimate the distances from the actual situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then try. Distance between you and me at this moment, were you farther away from the murder than the distance between the two of us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, somewhat further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Double that distance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's approximately what it was? Would the parties agree that it would be something, anything between 20 to 30 metres? My estimate of the distance of myself to this witness is approximately 12 metres. But you can measure it after -- after --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There are markings on the picture, so I think it's better to apply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but we're talking at this moment about the estimates of the witness in accuracy, may be in distances, may be in markings, can be else -- anywhere. I just wanted to focus on this alone at this moment. Mr. Lukic, you're looking at the clock, yes. So am I. Witness, we'll adjourn for the day. Mr. Lukic will need tomorrow most likely another 40 to 45 minutes. Mr. Lukic, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'd like to see you back tomorrow, but I can announce already to everyone that Courtroom I is again fully operational, which means that we would like to see you tomorrow morning in Courtroom I at 9.30. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 2nd of May, at 9.30 in the morning in Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of May, 2013, at 9.30 a.m. 22 23 24 25
